correctness.rationale: The class-two identities force every commutator to be a power of the basic commutator z=[a,b], so G' is cyclic. If c=|z|, centrality of a^i b^j is equivalent to c dividing both exponents, which gives G/Z(G)=C_c x C_c exactly. The commutator becomes the determinant pairing modulo c, proving the graph blow-up. The kernel of the determinant functional at a vector with gcd d has size cd, and Jordan's second totient counts the vectors in each gcd stratum. The graph recovers the center as its universal vertices and then c from |G|=|Z(G)|c^2. The explicit quotient and derived-subgroup maps preserve the determinant commutator and therefore give isoclinism. The packaged checker independently verifies the model groups and degree histograms.

originality.rationale: Broche--del Río give a much finer isomorphism classification of two-generated class-two p-groups for the modular group-algebra problem, but no commuting-graph theorem in the inspected material. Arvind--Cameron explicitly conjecture that class-two groups with the same commuting graph are isoclinic and prove only special cases such as extraspecial groups. The accepted result proves that conjecture for the entire two-generated class-two family and strengthens it to an exact graph classification and degree distribution. Targeted database and web searches under equivalent formulations found no covering theorem.
residual_risks: An equivalent theorem may exist in older literature on class-two groups under the language of alternating commutator maps or centralizer sizes rather than commuting graphs.
The 2025 cyclic-by-abelian result is related but structurally different; further unpublished or thesis-level work could overlap.
Standard facts about two-generated class-two groups are not claimed as new.
Failed searches do not prove novelty.

value.rationale: The theorem proves an explicit commuting-graph/isoclinism conjecture on a complete natural family rather than isolated examples. It identifies the entire graph, not only a scalar invariant, and gives a closed degree distribution for arbitrary composite or prime-power commutator order. The explicit order-32 collision also demonstrates sharply why isoclinism, rather than group isomorphism, is the correct reconstruction endpoint.
